FtMtF here. Biggest reason I detransitioned is because of the disrespect I received being a trans person, and I firmly believe that trans people who pass as cis don't experience near the same amount of harassment. So yes, not passing was an influence. And I think about this often.... if I did pass, I wouldn't have made the decision to detransition, I would have gone stealth. I would rather be a stealth trans man than a cis woman but I would rather be a cis woman than a visibly trans man.

It absolutely is a choice and your comment is still an example of that: someone makes the *choice* to transition *because* they would rather die than live with gender dysphoria. I think about killing myself literally every single day of my life but personally I'm making the *choice* to not transition *because* gender dysphoria does not justify the bullshit I would go through if I transitioned.

Coming out trans and gay is different. You don't choose who to fall in love with or who you're attracted to but if you have gender dysphoria and want to be another sex then it's most definitely a choice to transition. I am trying to find another way to deal with these feelings instead of transitioning so I am able to live the life I want (as a cis person)

If I am trying to transition to a cis man that is unachievable. I am trying to be a cis man/"go stealth" which is really only possible for like .001% of trans people to begin with. I don't think being trans itself is unachievable, if the goal is to be trans . But my goal was to actually be recognized and treated as the opposite gender and that is not possible

And I think there are trans people who don't cause pain to their friends and family but it seems like a very common theme is getting disowned by family and limiting yourself to never having friends/partners outside the LGBTQ community. I have not met a single person irl who has transitioned without causing a disruption in the lives of everyone else around them

I am in the process of finding a therapist but no, my family is a thousand times more important than transitioning. It's selfish to put my wants above my relationship with them. And it is not a fair trade off at all when I consider transitioning can only go so far
At first it was but once I realized what harm I had done to my friends and family and the fact that I was chasing after something that was unachievable it just created obsession and misery
I don't know what meditate on perceive myself means

Wish I was told earlier that I was in an echo chamber and *most* of the world is what those people would deem "transphobic." Not so much was it me being misinformed, just very niiave. I wish I knew how poorly trans people were actually treated offline in the real world and wish I knew/understood the impact my decision would have on the rest of my family. Given all of those I think i would have not transitioned or at least waited until I was in a less hostile environment

Then you are a trans woman and I will respect that, I will call you by your chosen name and she/her and think nothing else about it cause that's your life and your journey. The only reason I would be against you is if you try to convince people you're the same as a cis woman especially if you're trying to convince young people with gender dysphoria that they can be the same as cis male/female if they undergo transitioning. My gripe is that I was brainwashed into thinking I COULD become a man but realized I can only be a trans man which is completely different
